audit.reasoning: Quote verified verbatim in a held copy of the deciding source (Edwards 2021 p.35), which the record failed to link because the PDF sits under term1237/src rather than bilb1242 (we have no copy and grade/cite/loc fields empty). The source is a 2021 specialist synthesis by an author with his own Bilbaa field data, and the only older description in scope (Jonker 1915 sec. 4, held) states the same penult rule with no suffix-induced shift. Nothing Bilba-specific and nothing better exists per Glottolog (0 descriptive refs) and the reachable web. Coding 'penult primary, alternating secondary leftward' (stress placement coded per word length as 10 010 1010 01010 (1 = a stressed syllable)) matches the quote exactly. Weakness is only that the statement is cluster-level (all Rote lects) from a dictionary's background chapter rather than a Bilba phonology, hence 'adequate' not 'well-sourced'. sources.citation: Edwards 2021, Rote-Meto Comparative Dictionary, ANU Press, section 2.4 phonology of the Rote varieties incl. Bilbaa (full PDF re-read)
sources.quote: Content words contain at least two vowels. Some functors, such as the conjunction ma ‘and’, are monosyllabic. Stress falls on the penultimate vowel of a word with secondary stress assigned to every second syllable to the left.
